text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* In an interview, trade unions' leader Sergio Cofferati says the ruling majority together with hard-left Communist Refoundation party should reach an agreement over the mini-budget, the 1998 budget and welfare state reforms. This agreement should define government policy from now to the end of 1998 (Corriere della Sera).

* Majority parties are split over the proposal, backed by leftist PDS and Communist Refoundation party, of taxing severance pay. The measure would collect 5 trillion lire for the 16 trillion lire mini-budget aimed at cutting Italy's public deficit (all).

* The government is expected to issue in the next few days a decree law liberalising the Italian telecommunications market. Foreign groups will be allowed to bid for licences as telecom operators putting an end to the monopoly of Telecom Italia (La Repubblica).

* Fiat will reportedly take a stake in banking group Istituto San Paolo di Torino which is due to be privatised from its public foundation this year. The Turin-based car maker has so far ruled out any interest in the bank (Repubblica - Affari & Finanza).
* Seven Italian soccer teams (Lazio, Bologna, Fiorentina, Inter, Parma, Juventus and Milan AC) are reportedly planning to float on the London and Milan stock exchanges (La Stampa).
** reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
